title: What is known about 1RB0LB_1RC0LA_1LB0RD_1RE1RD_1RB1RF_1LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LB_1RC0LA_1LB0RD_1RE1RD_1RB1RF_1LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. At each new cell on the right the tape is 2 3^16 5 3 5 3^a1 5 3^a2 ... 5 3^am TAIL (lengths of runs of 1s), and the counts ai follow a closed-form law Pn → Qn → Rn → Pn+1, checked against direct simulation on every event to 109 steps. An exact model of the whole tape as one ternary counter, read at the left end and run with counter macros (16 November 2026), follows the machine through the first collapse (2.5×1018 steps), through the middle collapse the law predicted (it comes at 2.06×1035 steps, not at the fitted 4×1034) and on to 8.2×1051 steps, with no halt. The next collapse, when the oldest segment of the third regime runs out, is due near 1054 to 1055 steps and has not been reached.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 294,091 cells have been visited and 168,784 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.512). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.028).

claims.title: 16 shift rules
claims.text: For every n, the head crosses n copies of a short word in a fixed number of steps per copy and leaves another word behind (for example A going left over 0111 leaves 0100, 8 steps a copy; these are the moves that cross the 111-blocks of the counter). Generated and proved by bbtools.symtm, checked by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: The regime law, every event to 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: From step 223,270 on, every new cell written on the right in state D or F (16 events up to 10<sup>9</sup> steps) has exactly the list of segment lengths that the law P<sub>n</sub>, Q<sub>n</sub>, R<sub>n</sub> predicts, with g<sub>n</sub> = 2·3<sup>n+5</sup>−28, y<sub>n</sub>(j) = 3<sup>j+2</sup>(17−n+j)−27, c<sub>n</sub> = 161−2n.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2.29×10<sup>20</sup> steps, through the first collapse
claims.text: The macro simulator (blocks of 4 cells, crossing long runs of equal blocks in one go; exact, and it agrees with the direct simulator at 2×10<sup>9</sup> steps) ran 55 minutes from blank tape to step 229,416,990,524,183,704,810 without a halt. Every right-end event up to P<sub>14</sub> lies on the law, and P<sub>14</sub>, at step 2,515,258,871,431,441,221, is exactly the predicted list: the oldest segment is down to 0 and the end counter is 133. The run then leaves the law, as predicted, passes the collapse without halting, and the next new cell on the right comes at step 16,989,897,072,297,977,885 with the end counter at 204; 3 such events are recorded after the collapse.

claims.title: After the collapse: the next one (forecast)
claims.text: The law only looks at a segment's distance from the right end, so the right end of P13 was simulated beforehand from a shortened tape with 3, 4 or 5 kept segments. That forecast said the run would pass the collapse at P14 without halting and that the end counter would jump from 133 to 204; the full exact run has now done exactly that (previous claim). The same shortened runs say that in the second regime the oldest segment (321 blocks) loses about 9 per cycle, so the next collapse would be some 36 generations later, near 1046 steps. The second regime has no law yet, and nothing is known about that second collapse. (16 November 2026: superseded; the law puts the next collapse in the middle of the tape near 4×1034 steps, see below.)

claims.title: The general event law and the first collapse, reproduced (16 November 2026)
claims.text: At right-end D/F records the list [g, y<sub>1</sub>..y<sub>s</sub>, c] follows birth, drain, drain: birth [g,y,c] → [2·3<sup>s+4</sup>−28, g−3<sup>s+1</sup>+1, y<sub>i</sub>−3<sup>j+1</sup>, c], drain [g+2·3<sup>s+3</sup>, y<sub>i</sub>−3<sup>j+1</sup>, c−1] (j = segments to the right). The collapse at P<sub>14</sub>, simulated exactly on reduced tapes with 4, 5 and 6 kept segments and spliced into the full list (newborn entries fitted as A·3<sup>s</sup>+B, hidden segments drained by 10 events), gives exactly the real list at step 16,989,897,072,297,977,885, and all later records of the exact run match the law continued from it (end counter within 2). The record simulator agrees with direct simulation on all 49 records to 2×10<sup>8</sup> steps.

claims.title: The next collapse is in the middle, forecast near 4×10<sup>34</sup> steps
claims.text: Continued by the law, the list reaches P event 105 with every segment equal to a·3j+1−27, coefficients from the left 51, 48, …, 9, 24, 2, 35, 426, 399, …, 75 and end counter 170. At event 107 the segment with a = 2 (18th of 35, born at the first collapse) goes negative: a collapse in the middle of the tape, not at the right end, and it comes before the oldest segment or the end counter runs out. The step count there is about 0.4654·g2 with g = 300,189,270,593,998,214 (a fit), about 4×1034. This replaces the 1046 forecast below. (16 November 2026: the whole-tape run below finds the collapse at 2.06×1035 steps; the fit was off.)
claims.where: python3 holdouts/1RB0LB_1RC0LA_1LB0RD_1RE1RD_1RB1RF_1LA---/py/track.py b1 200 LOG (stops there with a note)

claims.title: The middle collapse in a cut-down window: no halt, not resolved
claims.text: Exact runs of a window around the dying segment (3 or 7 neighbours on the left, 3 on the right, a canonical generator in front, end counter 170) do not halt (the longer one to 1.15×1019 steps) but never come back to the law: the generator region is merged into the collapse, so the left part of the tape cannot be cut off. What the real collapse does, and whether it can halt, is not known. (Resolved by the whole-tape run below.)

claims.title: The whole tape as one exact counter (16 November 2026)
claims.text: Read at the left end, where the head bounces between right-end records, the tape is one ternary counter: runs of blocks 1000 (mirrored) separated by walls Z, O, T (digits 0, 1, 2) and a few other walls near births and collapses. Each bounce is a symbolic run of the machine on a window holding the carry (cdigits.py); every sample of the direct run to 107 steps (12,348 sweeps; 4,655 to 2×106 for the twin) equals the model. Counter macros (tacc.py) stand for exactly the sweeps they replace, step counts included: checked against plain sweeps on 5.07 million sweeps.

claims.title: No halt in the first 8.2×10<sup>51</sup> steps, through the middle collapse
claims.text: The accelerated whole-tape run reproduces the law events, the first collapse and the earlier exact msim records (the state at 1.7×1019 steps, run on by the independent block simulator c/msimev.c, gives the same tapes at the three later records of data/b1_far.txt, to 7.4×1019). The middle collapse comes at 2.060×1035 steps: the segment of coefficient 2 runs out, its two neighbours merge (473,513,913 and 2,841,083,638 blocks become 3,314,597,534), the counter passes a stretch of mixed digits and settles into a third regime of the same kind. No halt there, and none to 8.2×1051 steps. In the third regime each generation takes about 9 times as long as the last, the end counter drops by 2 per generation and the oldest segment by 9.
claims.where: BLAST=1000 MEMO_MAX=300000 SPEC_MEMO_MAX=300000 FULLLOG=LOG python3 holdouts/1RB0LB_1RC0LA_1LB0RD_1RE1RD_1RB1RF_1LA---/py/tacc.py run 1e6 SECONDS CKPT.pkl, python3 holdouts/1RB0LB_1RC0LA_1LB0RD_1RE1RD_1RB1RF_1LA---/py/farcheck.py b1

claims.title: 8 sweeps of the digit model, for all run lengths
claims.text: The 8 most used sweeps of the direct run to 2×10<sup>6</sup> steps, mirrored back to the machine's own orientation and proved for all lengths of the long runs and every tape beyond the window, checked by Lean's kernel (about a minute).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Halting needs the head in state D on a 0 with 1 1 to its right (D0 → 1RE, E1 → 1RF, F1 halts). Neither the law, nor the first collapse, nor the middle collapse (exact whole-tape run) produces it. The next event is the oldest segment of the third regime running out (26 blocks at 8.2×1051 steps, 9 fewer per generation), about 3 generations later, near 1054 to 1055 steps: a collapse of the same kind as the first one. The run has not got there yet.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LC_1LA0RD_1RA0LA_1RE1RD_1RA1RF_1LC--- up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet, but its run is understood exactly far beyond any direct simulation. The tape is a list of counters that drain at rates 3, 9, 27, … while new ones are born at the far end. Counters run out one after another, and each time the machine has settled into a new pattern of the same kind instead of halting: at 2.5×10<sup>18</sup> steps, at 2.06×10<sup>35</sup> and, so far, all the way to 8.2×10<sup>51</sup> steps. This page explains the counters, the law they follow and what is proved.

facts.text: No halt (exact whole-tape accelerated run), through two collapses.
The law matches direct simulation on every event to 10<sup>9</sup> steps.
Where the law ends: the oldest counter runs out there, as predicted, and the run goes on.

sections.heading: A list of counters on the tape
html: Each time the head writes a new cell at the right end of the tape (in state D or F), the tape reads, as lengths of runs of 1s with single 0s between them, 2 3^16 5 3 5 3^a1 5 3^a2 5 … 5 3^am TAIL. So it is mostly blocks 111, cut into segments by markers 11111; the numbers a1, …, am of blocks per segment are the whole state of the machine. Between two such moments the head sweeps over the whole tape, so a step of the list costs time proportional to the tape length.

Its relabelling 1RB0LC_1LA0RD_1RA0LA_1RE1RD_1RA1RF_1LC--- is this table started in state B (A→C, B→A, C→B), a different run; the two follow the same law, with one constant changed (c0 = 161 here, 38 there).

sections.heading: An exact law, three events per generation
html: The events come in threes, Pn, Qn, Rn. At Pn the list is [gn, yn(n), …, yn(0), cn] with gn = 2·3n+5−28, yn(j) = 3j+2(17−n+j)−27 and cn = 161−2n. Going from one event to the next, the segment that has i segments on its right loses 3i-ish blocks (exactly 3k+1−i with k = n+1), the end counter c loses 1 every other event, and the first segment gains 2·3k+4; every second generation step opens a new segment. Young segments are big and drain fast; old ones are small and drain slowly.

Each generation takes about 9 times as long as the one before. The law was found from simulation; it is checked on every event of the direct run to 109 steps and on every snapshot of an accelerated run to 2.8×1017 steps, but not proved for all n.

sections.heading: The oldest counter is a fuse
html: The oldest segment yn(0) = 9(17−n)−27 shrinks by 9 every generation: 126, 117, 108, …, 9 at P13, 0 at P14 (step 2.5×1018). One event later the law would need a negative count, so the pattern has to change: a collapse. Simulating just the right end beforehand (the law says the left part does not matter there) showed the machine surviving the collapse and settling into a new regime of the same kind with new numbers. On 13 November the full exact run got there: P14 came at step 2,515,258,871,431,441,221 with the oldest segment at 0, as predicted; the machine did not halt, and the next new cell on the right came at step 16,989,897,072,297,977,885 with the end counter at 204, the forecast value. The run has been followed to 2.29×1020 steps. The forecast for the new regime is that its own fuse burns out roughly 36 generations later, near 1046 steps.

The machine halts only if the head ever stands in state D on a 0 with 1 1 to its right. Inside a regime that never happens, so the question is what the collapses do: a halting proof or a non-halting proof needs a rule for them, and none is known yet.

sections.heading: The whole tape as one counter: through the middle collapse
html: The law above only looks at the right end. To follow the machine through a collapse in the middle of the tape, the whole tape was modelled instead, read at the left end, where the head turns between two right-end records. There the tape is one ternary counter: runs of the block 0001 separated by walls that stand for the digits 0, 1 and 2. Each bounce of the head sends a carry through it. One bounce is computed by running the machine symbolically on a window around the carry, long runs kept as variables, so every step is a real step of the machine; every sample of the direct run to 107 steps agrees with the model. Bounces are then stacked into counter macros (one macro: all bounces until a carry reaches a given digit), each derived once and reused, which is what lets the run cover 1050 steps in hours. The run reproduces the earlier exact records at 1.7, 4.2 and 7.4×1019 steps tape for tape.

The middle collapse comes at 2.06×1035 steps (the law's fit had said 4×1034). The segment that runs out leaves a short wall behind, its two neighbours merge into one, the counter passes a stretch of mixed digits and then settles into a third regime of the same kind as the first two: each generation about 9 times longer than the last, the end counter down by 2 per generation, the oldest segment down by 9. No halt comes anywhere near. The next collapse is due when that oldest segment runs out, about three generations after 8.2×1051 steps, near 1054 to 1055; it is of the same kind as the first one, which the machine survived.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.512). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.028).
After 109 steps the tape spans 294,091 cells (200,163 left of the start, 154 right), with a density of 1s of 0.574.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A nested ternary counter: the tape is a list of segments of 111-blocks drained by 3<sup>j</sup> per event; segments run out one after another (collapses), and after each the counter settles into a new regime of the same kind. An exact whole-tape run passes the first collapse (2.5×10<sup>18</sup> steps) and the middle collapse (2.06×10<sup>35</sup>) without halting and reaches 8.2×10<sup>51</sup> steps; the next collapse is due near 10<sup>54</sup> to 10<sup>55</sup>.
family: Nested ternary counter with an exact regime law (segments drained by 3^j per event)
